purpose: Bounded 2010-2012-2014 CCES panel ledger connecting earlier health-insurance status to later institutional approval, congressional contact, and local political action while preserving coverage timing, attribution, remedy, recovery, and exit as open.

events.geography: United States; retained 2010-2012-2014 CCES panel respondents
events.date_precision: 2012 panel wave; insurance status is a survey status and not a dated coverage-loss event
events.denominator: 912 respondents reporting no insurance and 8,587 reporting some insurance; outcome-specific valid counts vary
events.method: Same-respondent weighted descriptive comparison using the supplied CCES panel weight; no replicate-weight variance or causal estimate
events.missingness: Coverage start/end, bill, denial, care need, income, employment, alternatives, attribution, remedy, recovery, prior political identity, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Reported no health insurance in 2012 versus some form of insurance
events.alternatives_before_action: Employer coverage, public coverage, private purchase, family coverage, care non-use, and household resources are not observed for the same respondent
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The screen identifies insurance status but not a bill, care delay, financial loss, or health outcome
events.choice_or_response: In 2014, 31.75% of the no-insurance group reported congressional contact and 21.81% reported local political action, versus 40.29% and 32.48% among insured respondents
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employers, insurers, public programs, households, and Congress may shape coverage and political routes, but authority for an individual status is not identified
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: 2014 Congress approval, congressional contact, and local political action are observed as separate downstream measures; no coverage remedy or institutional correction is verified
events.durability_followup: No later coverage restoration, health care use, household security, trust change, continued dependence, switching, or exit is linked
events.immediate_outcome: The same panel places insurance status before later institution-specific judgment, contact, and local political action
events.protected_outcome: Political contact or action may express voice, but no protected health, financial, or institutional outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Lower observed contact and action may reflect constrained time, resources, access, or competing pressures, but the mechanism is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The panel does not identify whether coverage costs or care risks shifted to the household, employer, insurer, or public system
events.later_outcome: Favorable Congress approval was 11.51% after no insurance versus 10.23% among insured respondents; unfavorable approval was 74.77% versus 83.07%
events.meaning_and_attribution: Congress approval is institution-specific and may reflect prior identity or expectations; blame, fairness, control, and trust change are not identified
events.public_or_collective_response: Congressional contact and a composite of local meeting, sign, campaign work, or donation are reported; issue, organizing sequence, and response are not observed
events.counterexample: Lower contact/action alongside slightly higher favorable approval does not prove withdrawal, distrust, or a health-policy mechanism
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained 9,499-row CCES panel reproduction and canonical trend record; supplied panel weight is descriptive, attrition and causal identification are unresolved, and insurance status is not a dated shock

arrows.evidence: The panel classifies insurance status but does not contain a dated bill, care episode, or later household-security measure in this compact route
arrows.counterexample: Noncoverage may be stable status, temporary transition, or a result of other resources rather than a shock
arrows.remaining_gap: Coverage timing, bill/denial, care need, payment, non-use, health outcome, and recovery

arrows.evidence: The same retained respondents are observed in 2014 on favorable and unfavorable Congress approval
arrows.counterexample: Approval may reflect prior party identity, national events, or expectations rather than coverage status
arrows.remaining_gap: Prior approval/identity, attribution, fairness, and a dated coverage-to-judgment design

arrows.evidence: Any congressional contact is observed in 2014 for the same panel respondents: 31.75% versus 40.29%
arrows.counterexample: Contact purpose, access, institutional response, and resolution are not observed
arrows.remaining_gap: Issue, effort, recipient response, remedy, and subsequent trust or repeat contact

arrows.evidence: The same panel reports local meeting, sign, campaign-work, or donation activity in 2014: 21.81% versus 32.48%
arrows.counterexample: A lower composite action share does not identify time scarcity, issue mismatch, withdrawal, or lack of alternatives
arrows.remaining_gap: Action sequence, issue attribution, organizing, voting, withdrawal, and mechanism

arrows.to: coverage remedy, care recovery, trust change, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The retained panel screen ends at 2014 political outcomes and contains no linked remedy, recovery, trust-change, switching, or exit endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Political contact or action can coexist with unresolved coverage, and non-action can reflect constraint rather than satisfaction
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated institutional response, coverage/care recovery, later trust, continued dependence, switching, withdrawal, and exit

boundary: This ledger strengthens the same-panel insurance-status to institutional-judgment-and-action bridge, but it does not establish a dated coverage loss, causal effect, attribution, remedy, recovery, trust change, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact published/reproduced panel estimates, source URL, denominators, and interpretation limits are retained; the local raw panel file remains outside Git.
